# two_templates_cut.col - the same file, cut off mid row group
#
# two_templates.col cut at byte 979 (0x3d3), half way through row group 2's
# chunk area: what a crash leaves when it lands inside a write. There is no trailer, so
# the file is unsealed and a reader walks it frame by frame from the header.
#
# Row group 2's header frame at 0x317 is whole and its CRC holds, but its chunk
# area needs 96 bytes and 48 remain, so the walk stops there.
# Recovery truncates the file to 791 bytes (0x317), which keeps both schema
# records, row groups 0 and 1 and the optional frame, writes a footer and trailer, and
# seals it. Six rows survive:
#   template 101, schema 0: {"http.status":200,"level":"INFO","order_id":"0045000012","ts":"2024-01-15T16:00:00.120+05:30"}
#   template 101, schema 0: {"http.status":"404","level":"WARN","order_id":"0045000013","ts":"2024-01-15T16:00:01.000+05:30"}
#   template 101, schema 0: {"http.status":503,"level":"ERROR","order_id":"0045000014","ts":"2024-01-15T16:00:01.250+05:30"}
#   template 102, schema 1: {"@timestamp":"2024-01-15T10:30:00.5Z","client.ip":"10.0.0.1","latency":0.25,"ok":true,"req.id":"550E8400-E29B-41D4-A716-446655440000","ts_ms":1705314600500}
#   template 102, schema 1: {"@timestamp":"2024-01-15T10:30:00.25Z","client.ip":"2001:db8::1","latency":1.5,"ok":"True","req.id":"6BA7B810-9DAD-11D1-80B4-00C04FD430C8","ts_ms":1705314600250}
